title: Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds
abstract: arXiv:2611.08495v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Instruction tuning of large language models and large vision language models relies on massive training data, which incurs substantial computational and storage costs. Meanwhile, training data often contains redundancy, noise, and low quality samples. Existing data selection methods mostly rely on diversity, importance, or a combination of both, without explicitly constraining the distributional consistency between the selected subset and the full data in the embedding space. We propose QMAC, a quality aware multiband characteristic function matching method that formulates data selection as a joint optimization problem of distribution matching and quality filtering. QMAC matches the empirical characteristic functions of the selected subset and the full data across multiple frequency scales, capturing both global semantic coverage and local perturbations, while using task related quality scores to filter noisy and low quality samples. translated_title: 重新思考数据选择：作为语义流形上的分布匹配问题
tldr: 该论文提出QMAC方法，将数据选择重新表述为语义流形上分布匹配与质量过滤的联合优化问题，通过在多个频率尺度上匹配特征函数来同时捕捉全局语义覆盖与局部扰动，从而高效筛选出高质量、高代表性的训练数据子集。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes QMAC, which reformulates data selection as a joint optimization of distribution matching and quality filtering on semantic manifolds, matching empirical characteristic functions across multiple frequency scales to capture both global semantic coverage and local perturbations for selecting high-quality, representative training data subsets.
